probes.label: Accessor names, lengths and nonconstructibility
probes.source: let symbol=Symbol("slot");let o={get x(){return 1;},set x(v){},get [symbol](){return 2;}};let d=Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(o,"x"),s=Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(o,symbol);test.record(d.get.name);test.record(d.set.name);test.record(d.get.length);test.record(d.set.length);test.record(s.get.name);test.record(Object.hasOwn(d.get,"prototype"));try{new d.get();}catch(e){test.record(e.name);}test.record(s.get.call(o));let get=3,set=4;let plain={get,set};test.record(plain.get+plain.set);let methods={get(){return 5;},set(v){return v;}};test.record(methods.get()+methods.set(6));

probes.label: Array length descriptors and batched definitions
probes.note: Array length stays nonenumerable/nonconfigurable and participates in defineProperty/defineProperties.

probes.label: Array shrinking deletes indices while preserving named properties
probes.note: Shrinking removes existing elements beyond the new length; holes and named properties retain their distinct behavior.

probes.label: Descending shrink stops at a nonconfigurable index

probes.label: Nonwritable length blocks new out-of-range indices
probes.note: Nonwritable length rejects extension but permits otherwise valid definitions of existing indices.

probes.label: Length conversion order and invalid numeric lengths
probes.note: Array length definition performs specified numeric conversions and rejects inconsistent or fractional results before mutation.

probes.label: Accessor indices update length and expose ordinary descriptors
probes.note: Numeric accessor definitions extend array length and are deleted by a valid shrink.

probes.label: Strict writes and native mutators observe length descriptors
probes.source: let a=[1,2];Object.defineProperty(a,"length",{writable:false});function strictLength(){"use strict";a.length=1;}try{strictLength();}catch(e){test.record(e.name);}try{a.push(3);}catch(e){test.record(e.name);}try{a.pop();}catch(e){test.record(e.name);}test.record(a.length);test.record(1 in a);let b=[1,2,3];Object.defineProperty(b,"1",{configurable:false});b.length=0;test.record(b.length);test.record(2 in b);function strictShrink(){"use strict";b.length=0;}try{strictShrink();}catch(e){test.record(e.name);}test.record(b.length);

probes.label: Boxed primitive construction, identity and coercion
probes.source: let n=new Number(7),b=new Boolean(false),s=Symbol('box'),w=Object(s);test.record(Object(n)===n);test.record(new Object(n)===n);test.record(Object(7)!==Object(7));test.record(n.valueOf());test.record(new Number().valueOf());test.record(new Boolean().valueOf());test.record(Number(n));test.record(Boolean(b));test.record(typeof w);test.record(w.valueOf()===s);test.record(Object.getPrototypeOf(n)===Number.prototype);test.record(Object.getPrototypeOf(b)===Boolean.prototype);test.record(Object.getPrototypeOf(w)===Symbol.prototype);test.record(n instanceof Number);test.record(b instanceof Boolean);test.record(w instanceof Symbol);
probes.note: Wrappers preserve internal primitive values and object identity; wrapping an existing object does not replace it.

probes.label: Intrinsic primitive slots and branded method receivers
probes.note: Only genuine internal slots satisfy branded methods; Number/Boolean intrinsic prototypes have the standard primitive values.

probes.label: Primitive receiver boxing and strict receiver preservation
probes.source: function receiver(){return this;}function strictReceiver(){'use strict';return this;}let n=receiver.call(5),b=receiver.call(false),s=Symbol('this'),w=receiver.call(s);test.record(typeof n);test.record(n.valueOf());test.record(n instanceof Number);test.record(b.valueOf());test.record(b instanceof Boolean);test.record(w.valueOf()===s);test.record(receiver.call(5)!==receiver.call(5));test.record(strictReceiver.call(5)===5);test.record(strictReceiver.call(false)===false);test.record(strictReceiver.call(s)===s);let bound=receiver.bind(4);test.record(bound().valueOf());test.record(bound()!==bound());
probes.note: Non-strict calls box Number/Boolean/Symbol receivers per invocation; strict and bound-call semantics retain their required identities.

probes.label: Symbol wrappers, property keys and ordinary integrity
probes.note: A Symbol wrapper remains an object with expandos and integrity while its primitive key identity is retained.

probes.label: JSON primitive-wrapper conversion and ordinary Symbol objects
probes.note: JSON unwraps Number/Boolean values using the required conversion rules; Symbol wrappers serialize ordinary own fields.

probes.label: Default, numeric and string conversion hints
probes.note: Addition/equality use default, numeric operators use number and property keys/string conversion use string.

probes.label: Hook lookup, fallback, exception identity and result checks
probes.note: The hook is read once; null/undefined fall back, non-callables and object results reject, and thrown values propagate.

probes.label: Inherited hooks, original receivers and Symbol return values
probes.note: Inherited conversion hooks see the original receiver; Symbol results remain Symbol keys and obey subsequent string/number restrictions.

probes.label: Existing native helpers share ordered conversion hooks
probes.note: Math, character construction, parsing, joins, typed storage and length conversion all observe the supported conversion protocol.

probes.label: Well-known Symbol identity and intrinsic conversion method
probes.note: The well-known key and Symbol prototype hook expose the standard immutable key, function metadata and branded receiver behavior.
